column1: # What a change can break: the one map of the CI workflow and of `scripts/ci.sh affected` (docs/RELEASE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md).
# `=NAME<TAB>ERE` names a group of job names of scripts/ci.sh (`scripts/ci.sh --plan`). Any other row is `PATH<TAB>JOBS`: PATH is an ERE over a changed file,
# JOBS an ERE over job names in which {NAME} stands for a group and \N for a group of PATH; `-` means no job (the file is mapped, nothing runs), `.` every job. A file
# takes the union of the rows it matches. A file that no row matches runs every job. The names `gh:sqlite`, `gh:mariadb`, `gh:replication` and `gh:macos` are the
# workflow jobs that are not in scripts/ci.sh. `scripts/ci.sh --selftest` fails when a tracked file matches no row or a job is in no group, so a new
# test or file is never left out silently. The nightly run and the release check run every job: this map only picks what a push runs.
# A row whose JOBS start with `fast:` is read only by the fast tier of a pull request (`scripts/ci.sh affected --github`, `fastjobs`): a file it matches runs
# the regression tests of its own area there, not of the whole stack above it; the push to main and the nightly run use the rows below, which run the stack.
# groups (a job may be in several: the stack col, agg and table is one chain of code, so a change of one runs the groups above it)
# the search the other areas call
# what the fast tier of a pull request runs besides the tests of the area: the proof of the coverage table and the emulated isolation tests (a few seconds each)
# the whole build and every harness: a change here can break anything
# the CI machinery: it runs every job, and builds nothing the focused performance gate measures
# the fast tier: the tests of the area of a source file (the stack above it, and the other versions, run on the push to main)
# nothing the jobs build or run: release, packaging, benchmarks, documentation, tools, the other workflows
# Focused performance uses the groups above; shared build/SQL cover every group. {perf} marks what cannot change the extension it builds twice
# (the gate, its selector, the CI machinery): identical builds measure only noise, so they select nothing (the nightly run still measures everything).
# {ci} marks the jobs a path can break but not slow: the tests are not built into the extension, and the SiftAgg code is not on the path of the storage cases
# (no grouped query, no table source scan; the aggregate cases read the table through it), so the aggregate stack above it is correctness-only for the gate.
